description: An agent skill for creating detailed, interactive isometric illustrations of real-world machines and complex systems. Generates polished SVGs with optional WebGL shaders and 3D effects.

summary.one_liner: An agent skill that makes Claude explain a technical idea by building it as a detailed, interactive isometric figure in SVG, with optional WebGL shaders and a beta 3D mode.
summary.what_it_does: Anatomy is a skill folder (SKILL.md plus a drawing kit) that directs a coding agent to turn a technical concept into a physical object whose working represents the idea, such as a lock whose pins must all match before it turns. The agent builds the object from many small shaded isometric parts and places it in a framed card with a title, hint and live readout tied to a small model. The figure moves under pointer and keyboard input, with eased motion. Output can be a standalone HTML page, a lone SVG file with embedded styles, or React/Next.js components. The SVG+WebGL mode adds shader layers for effects like fire, water and light, and a beta 3D mode re-projects moving parts each frame. The kit uses only Node built-in modules, and headless Chrome scripts take screenshots and run geometry audits. Examples in the repo include a dial indicator, a desk computer, an arcade cabinet, a raptor engine and a ripple tank.
use_cases: explain a technical concept with an illustrated machine
make an isometric SVG for docs or a blog post
create a React component illustration for a Next.js site
animated diagram of a mechanism with live readouts
add shader effects like fire or water to an SVG figure
how_to_run: In Claude Code: /anatomy explain how a token bucket rate limiter works, interactive
Optional build of an example: node examples/dial-indicator/build.mjs
Add --light to a build command for the light theme
notable: Turns abstract ideas into invented physical objects whose mechanics embody the concept
Every number shown comes from the same model that moves the parts
Includes a geometry audit that checks for parts passing through each other and depth order
Works across Claude Code, Antigravity, OpenCode, Codex and MiniMax Code
No API keys and no npm install needed for the kit
caveats: Not a chart library: no axes, series or data plots
Slow by design; a full figure takes a long session and the Raptor build takes a few minutes
Shaders need WebGL; the 3D mode is beta and proved on only one example and one test figure
Browser checks may be blocked by Codex's sandbox and need manual approval
